history.summary: Large 1647sqft 3BR at $1214 psf is roughly 21% below the River Isles URA median of $1536, anchoring a sub-$2M entry into a 610-unit Punggol development with a strong 7.66%/yr resale CAGR on 154 transactions. Walkable to Riviera MRT (480m) with Punggol Digital District and CRL as durable D19 catalysts. The deep PSF discount on an oversized layout is the standout: real upside if the unit is a normal (not penthouse-only) configuration.
history.rating_rationale: Best combination of value and momentum in the batch: $1214 psf vs $1536 median, 7.66%/yr URA appreciation backed by 154 resale-only transactions (high confidence), and a 610-unit development gives a deep buyer pool. Sub-$2M price sits in a liquid band for HDB upgraders. Qingjian build with 3.3/5 reviews (units close together, average interior finishing) caps it below Strong Buy, and the unusually low PSF on 1647sqft warrants verifying the layout isn't a hard-to-resell penthouse. Catalysts (PDD, CRL ~2030) are concrete.

history.summary: Large 1,647 sqft Punggol unit at a low $1,214 psf — but the cheapness is mostly a big-unit size effect on a thin 4-transaction cohort, and the $2.0M quantum sits at the illiquid top end of leasehold Punggol.
history.rating_rationale: River Isles' 12-month range is $1,310-$1,695 psf (avg ~$1,520), so on PSF this 1,647 sqft unit at $1,214 psf does screen cheap. But two things temper it: (1) psf_cohort_txns = 4 — a thin cohort the v3.4 prior says to distrust, and (2) at 1,647 sqft this is an unusually large layout (likely 4BR/dual-key or premium), and large units structurally trade at lower PSF, so much of the -30.4% age_adj and -18.4% psf_premium is a size artifact rather than true alpha. The $1,999,999 absolute quantum is the real concern: it is at the very top of the Punggol leasehold market, where 3BRs commonly transact around $1.2-1.5M — buyers at $2.0M in OCR leasehold are scarce, so exit liquidity is weak and price discovery thin. Project quality is fine (large land, full facilities, 2015 TOP) and the Cross Island Line (~2030, Hougang/Punggol connectivity) is a genuine regional catalyst, and OCR D19 has the strongest forward region prior. But a high-quantum, large-format unit on a 4-txn cohort is a near-tie with too much uncertainty to call a Buy. Neutral, low confidence.
red_flags: psf_cohort_txns = 4 — low PSF rests on very few comparables; the -18.4% discount is likely overstated
$1,999,999 quantum is at the illiquid top end of Punggol leasehold (typical 3BRs ~$1.2-1.5M) — weak exit liquidity
1,647 sqft is an oversized layout; low PSF is largely a size effect, not a genuine per-unit bargain
99-year lease from 2012 — lease decay plus far-OCR location compounds resale risk at a high quantum
catalysts: Cross Island Line (~2030, Hougang interchange) — confirmed dated connectivity catalyst for Punggol/D19
OCR D19 carries the strongest realized forward-return region prior; large family layout with full facilities on a big site
If a genuine dual-key, the layout could support rental flexibility (rent one key, occupy the other)

history.summary: A 1,647 sqft / 2-bath "3BR" at River Isles asking $1,999,999 ($1,214 psf). The developer's own unit mix identifies this as a 3-Bedroom PES/RT unit (1,152-2,088 sqft, 39 of 610 units) - a standard ~1,100 sqft 3-bedroom core plus ~500 sqft of unenclosed private-enclosed-space or roof terrace. Its low PSF is that outdoor area, not a discount: against River Isles' own >=1,550 sqft format class the ask is at mark-to-market, not below it.
history.rating_rationale:
The score_1000 of 803 is a format artifact and does not survive verification. Both of its drivers - age_value +15.65 (-22.1% vs the D19 age-adjusted median for the 1,400-1,800 sqft band) and psf_value +6.33 (-15.3% vs the project's own URA median) - benchmark a unit that is roughly a third unenclosed terrace/patio against ordinary fully-enclosed apartments. Qingjian's published mix confirms the format: 3-Bedroom PES/RT, 1,152-2,088 sqft, 39 units; 2 bathrooms matches the standard 893-1,184 sqft 3BR core, not a genuine 1,647 sqft apartment.

Priced against its own format the ask is fair, not cheap. Across 154 River Isles URA prints the >=1,550 sqft class has traded at a stable ~0.79-0.83x the psf of the standard 850-1,250 sqft stock every year since 2021 (0.83 / 0.85 / 0.88 / 0.78 / 0.79). Standard-stock median psf is $1,536 in 2026, so the format marks to ~$1,213-1,275 psf. The ask is $1,214. The one backtest-validated forward signal - cheap-vs-peers - therefore does not fire.

Worse, the format has measurably lagged the project it sits in. Like-for-like: 1,593 sqft went $1,004 psf (Jun-22) to $1,011 psf (Jan-24), +0.7%, while standard units went +19% over the same span; 1,937 sqft went $1,084 (Nov-23) to $1,169 (Mar-25), +7.8%, against ~+19%. The band ratio drifted 0.83 -> 0.79. Crediting this unit the project's trailing 7.66% CAGR - which is standard-stock-dominated - overstates it, and the run's $2.83M 5-year exit would be an 18% new all-time high for a project whose largest print ever is $2.40M.

It is also dominated inside its own development at the same money. In the last 10 months buyers paid $2.018M / $2.038M for 1,227 sqft 4BR/3-bath units and $2.25-2.30M for 1,475 sqft 4BR units - more bedrooms, more bathrooms, fully enclosed, 120-154 units per format instead of 39, and the faster-appreciating band. Paying $2.0M for three bedrooms and two bathrooms in Punggol is the weak side of that trade.

Carry is thin and exit is slow. URA rental filings for this project size the rent honestly at ~$4,675-5,000/mo (3BR 1,500-1,600 sqft n=2; 4BR 1,600-1,700 sqft n=3) - better than the run's $4,050 project-bed median, but still only ~2.9% gross and ~1.7% net on $2.0M. Re-scored at the OCR baseline with the size-matched rent, all-cash ROI is 3.8%/yr over 5 years, not the 6.9% the default run shows. The format prints roughly twice a year (11 prints in 5 years) and nothing in the 1,550-1,700 sqft range has transacted in 30 months, so a 5-7yr exit depends on finding one of the few buyers who specifically wants a patio.

River Isles itself is a decent OCR asset - 610 units, 916 lifetime transactions, standard stock compounding ~7.7%/yr since 2021, Punggol Digital District and the SIT campus underneath it. Nothing here is a trap or a mis-scrape. But at fair value, in the project's worst-performing and least liquid format, at the top of its quantum distribution, with ~2.9% carry and a strictly better substitute available in the same condo at the same price, there is no forward edge left once the artifact is removed. Avoid this unit; the project's standard 4BR stock is the listing worth watching.
red_flags: Format artifact, not value: this is a 3-Bedroom PES/RT unit (Qingjian's mix: 1,152-2,088 sqft, 39 of 610 units) - ~1,100 sqft enclosed 3BR core plus ~500 sqft of PES/roof terrace. Both MMR value components (age_value +15.65, psf_value +6.33) compare that area to fully-enclosed apartments. The -22.1% and -15.3% 'discounts' are the terrace.

Not cheap vs its own format: River Isles' >=1,550 sqft class trades at 0.79-0.83x the standard-stock psf every year since 2021. 2026 standard median $1,536 psf implies $1,213-1,275 psf for this format. The ask is $1,214 psf - mark-to-market, no discount.

The format has lagged the project: 1,593 sqft $1,004 psf (Jun-22) -> $1,011 psf (Jan-24) = +0.7% while standard stock rose ~19%; 1,937 sqft +7.8% (Nov-23 -> Mar-25) against ~19%. Band ratio drifted 0.83 -> 0.79. The project's 7.66% trailing CAGR is standard-stock-dominated and must not be applied to this unit.

Dominated inside its own development at the same money: 1,227 sqft 4BR/3-bath printed $2.018M (Oct-25), $2.080M (Dec-25), $2.038M (Mar-26); 1,475 sqft 4BR printed $2.25-2.30M (Sep-25 to Feb-26). More bedrooms, more baths, all enclosed, 120-154 units per format vs 39, and the faster band.
3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms at a $2.0M quantum. 1,647 sqft on 2 baths is 824 sqft/bath - the 4BR buyer at this price gets 3 baths. Narrow resale appeal at the top of the project's price range.

Format illiquidity: 11 prints >=1,550 sqft in 5 years (~2/yr) out of ~106 large units, and ZERO prints in the 1,550-1,700 sqft range in the last 30 months. psf_cohort_txns = 3 - the MMR's own comp basis is three transactions.
Quantum at the top of the book: $2.0M is ~p90 of 154 prints (median $1.389M, all-time max $2.40M). The run's $2.83M 5-year exit would be an 18% new project record.

Thin carry: size-matched URA rent ~$4,675-5,000/mo (3BR 1,500-1,600 sqft n=2 @ $4,675; 4BR 1,600-1,700 sqft n=3 @ $5,000) = ~2.9% gross, ~1.7% net. Re-scored at the OCR baseline with that rent, all-cash ROI is 3.8%/yr (5yr) / 4.0%/yr (7yr), not the 6.9% shown. Per priors, yield is carry and never appreciation.

LRT, not MRT: the record's '480m from CP3 Riviera MRT' is Riviera LRT (Punggol East Loop). Geocoding in --score puts the nearest true MRT at Punggol, 1,514m. MMR credits mrt +3.16 off the LRT distance - real daily convenience, but not an MRT premium.

Momentum -0.761 and the Punggol run is largely spent: standard-stock median psf $1,062 (2021) -> $1,536 (2026 YTD, n=6) is +45% already banked. External 2026 commentary expects north-east resale growth to moderate, with 3,200+ Punggol flats reaching MOP in 2026 adding upgrader-side supply.

Floor level and PES-vs-roof-terrace unconfirmed: PropertyGuru detail enrichment returned no floor_level (403 on direct fetch, Cloudflare), and there is no researched stack profile for River Isles. A ground-floor PES and a top-floor roof terrace are materially different products at the same strata area.
realsmart REALSCORE unavailable this run - see rental_assessment/appreciation_assessment notes; fields left null rather than guessed.
catalysts: The development itself is sound: 610 units, 916 lifetime transactions totalling $960.6M (realsmart /p page, latest 29 Jun 2026), standard stock compounding ~7.7%/yr since 2021 ($1,062 -> $1,536 psf median). A third-party listing page cites 99% profitable resales on 311 transactions - unverified against realsmart directly, but consistent with the print record showing no loss-making resales in the file.

OCR region - the favoured forward region in the backtest (realized +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%; config OCR baseline 4.2%). Real, but it is the baseline available in any OCR asset, not a River Isles edge.

Punggol Digital District (~28,000 jobs; UOB, OCBC, GovTech, CSA) plus the SIT campus sit directly behind this address - genuine live-work-study rental demand. Note the priors: the future-infrastructure channel has NO measured forward power, so this is story, not signal.

Genuine product for the right buyer: a large family unit with ~500 sqft of private outdoor space at $1,214 psf, 480m to Riviera LRT (3 stops to Punggol interchange), full facilities on a 9-tower, all north-south-oriented site. The outdoor area does earn rent - URA filings show 3BR 1,900-2,000 sqft at $5,200/mo vs $4,250 for a standard 1,100-1,200 sqft 3BR.
Lease is not an issue: 99 years from 6 Feb 2012 leaves ~85.5 years, ~79 at a 7-year exit - well clear of CPF pro-rating.

The ask is not above comps. This is a fair price, honestly set - the case against it is opportunity cost and format, not overpricing. If the format premium ever compresses toward the standard band, the same unit re-rates; nothing in five years of prints suggests it has started.
